_comment: GENERATED-BY-HAND ONCE, THEN FROZEN. Every number cites a source in `sources`; nothing here is estimated. The geometry comes from roller_rig's own generator metadata and C's own sweep, because a copy of a generator's number is one copy too many. The observability verdict is the output of experiments/dock_observability.py and REFUSES to certify the tight side of the window, which is why `certifies_tight_side` is false: the contract is written and it says out loud that it cannot yet clear a dock by ranging alone.

station_c.role: the C fixture: the fixed roller band (source) and the receiver band, with the vehicle's deck bridging them
station_c.declared_by: assets/world_p3_cell.xml, crown plane from roller_rig CROWN_Z

measured_bracket.note: discrete sweep points, so the boundary is bracketed between the last pass and the first fail; the asymmetry (+20 mm against -2 mm) is a measured property, not a margin choice

measurement_error_m.note: the smallest longitudinal step whose scan change clears the declared 5 mm noise floor

control_residual_m.note: the tight side of C's own bracket, i.e. how far out the chassis was when the transfer last succeeded

settling_drift_m.note: NOT MEASURED for the dock stage. Set to the tight side of the bracket so the sum cannot understate the budget; a real measurement is an open item

not_observable: any quantity below the 5 mm range resolution
anything dynamic: the gate is a static fan at one pose
observability.method: 2D lidar fan through the assembled world; pose-to-scan map tested for injectivity over a 7x7x7 grid
observability.why_not_certified: the sensor's smallest detectable longitudinal step is 5 mm and the tight side of C's window is 2 mm, so a dock 2 mm out cannot be distinguished from one on centre by ranging alone; the honest outcomes are a guiding chamfer, a compliance mechanism, or a sensor that measures the interface itself

sources.not_measured: declared as unmeasured on purpose; a placeholder that cites itself would look like a measurement
